title: From Projects to Asset Classes
subtitle: Two-stage finance and synthetic sovereign bonds for clean power
message: Clean power plants are financed one at a time, on bespoke terms. Split each project at commissioning, pool operating plants under one standard contract and refinance them through first loss, a thin mezzanine and a senior synthetic sovereign bond. Standardization, not subsidy, lowers the price.

problem.text: Once a payment intermediary removes buyer risk, the rest of the premium is packaging: each plant is financed alone, on bespoke documents, by a lender who carries its construction risk for twenty years and cannot sell the loan to a pension fund.

mechanism.title: Split at commissioning, then pool and tranche
mechanism.caption: Cost of power from the stylized plant, US c/kWh, with two years of construction interest.
points: Banks build against a contingent PPA; bond investors hold the operating plant.
Pool across countries; tranche into first loss, mezzanine and a senior bond.
4.8% subordination makes the senior bond near-AAA at correlation 0.10; 7.7% at 0.20.
A 5.65% blended cost gives 4.6 c/kWh against 6.2: 27% less.

action.title: Identical contracts make portfolios
results: A ten-country pool needs 5.3% subordination; one country needs 9.2%.
Guaranteeing the $460m mezzanine of a $10bn pool costs about $6m over ten years, but it can be fully drawn in a crisis.
With twice the defaults and 72% recovery, power still costs 4.7 c/kWh.
The host keeps a contingent liability.
